# Session Overview

{{< include /program/_session2.md >}}

## Session Objectives

This session focuses on building foundational skills in Quarto authoring, covering enhanced markdown capabilities, YAML configuration, and document structuring best practices.

## Learning Objectives

::: {.fragment fragment-index="1"}

By the end of this session, participants will be able to:

:::

- [Create well-structured documents using enhanced Quarto markdown features.]{.fragment fragment-index="2"}
- [Configure documents using YAML headers for different output formats.]{.fragment fragment-index="3"}
- [Use advanced formatting features including callouts, cross-references, and tabsets.]{.fragment fragment-index="4"}

# Markdown Basics

## Text Formatting Essentials

::: {.fragment fragment-index="1"}

Basic text formatting you'll use every day:

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index="2"}

- **Bold text** with `**bold**` or `__bold__`.
- *Italic text* with `*italic*` or `_italic_`.
- ***Bold and italic*** with `***text***`.
- Superscript^2^ with `superscript^2^`.
- Subscript~2~ with `subscript~2~`.
- `Verbatim code` with backticks.

:::

## Headers Structure Your Content

::: {.fragment fragment-index="1"}

Headers create your document structure and enable automatic table of contents generation.

```markdown
# Heading 1 - Document Title
## Heading 2 - Major Sections  
### Heading 3 - Subsections
#### Heading 4 - Minor Sections
##### Heading 5 - Rare Usage
###### Heading 6 - Very Rare
```

:::

::: {.callout-tip .fragment fragment-index="2"}
Add a empty lines before and after!
:::

## Lists

::: {.callout-important .fragment fragment-index="3"}
Quarto requires empty lines before and after lists to ensure proper rendering!
:::

::: {layout-ncol="2"}

::: {.fragment fragment-index="1"}

**Unordered Lists:**

```markdown
- First item
- Second item  
- Third item
```

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index="2"}

**Ordered Lists:**

```markdown
1. First step
2. Second step
3. Third step
```

:::

:::

## Lists - Nested {.smaller}

::: {.callout-important .fragment fragment-index="2"}
The number of spaces for indentation does not matter, but the list marker must be aligned with the first character of the parent item.
Items marked **bad** below show incorrect alignment of nested content.
:::

::: {layout-ncol="2"}

::: {.fragment fragment-index="1"}

````markdown
- First item

```r
print("Hello, World!")
```

-    Second item (**bad**)

  ::: {.callout-tip}
  Here is a tip!
  :::

        - Sub item

-    Third item

      ::: {.callout-tip}
      Here is a tip!
      :::

  - Sub item
````

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index="2"}

````markdown
- First item

  ```r
  print("Hello, World!")
  ```

-  Second item (**bad**)

   ::: {.callout-tip}
   Here is a tip!
   :::

   - Sub item

-    Third item

     ::: {.callout-tip}
     Here is a tip!
     :::

     - Sub item
````

:::

:::

## Working with Code {.smaller}

::: {.fragment fragment-index="1"}

**Inline code:** Use single backticks

```markdown
The `print()` function outputs text.
```

:::

::: {.callout-tip .fragment fragment-index="2"}
Code highlighting for inline code:

```markdown
The `print()`{.python} function outputs text.
```

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index="3"}

**Code blocks:** Use triple backticks with optional language

````markdown
```python
def hello_world():
    print("Hello, Quarto!")
```
````

:::

::: {.callout-note .fragment fragment-index="4"}

The syntax highlighting is provided by [`skylighting` {{< iconify octicon:mark-github-16 title="GitHub" label="GitHub" >}}](https://github.com/jgm/skylighting).

:::

## Tables Made Simple {.smaller}

::: {layout-ncol="2"}

::: {.fragment fragment-index="1"}

```markdown
| Default | Left | Right | Center |
|---------|:-----|------:|:------:|
| 12      | 12   |    12 |   12   |
| 123     | 123  |   123 |  123   |
| 1       | 1    |     1 |   1    |

: Demonstration of pipe table syntax
```

:::

::: {style="font-size: 50%;" .fragment fragment-index="2"}

| Default | Left | Right | Center |
|---------|:-----|------:|:------:|
| 12      | 12   |    12 |   12   |
| 123     | 123  |   123 |  123   |
| 1       | 1    |     1 |   1    |

: Demonstration of pipe table syntax

:::

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index="3"}

Use colons (`:`) to control alignment:

- `:---` for left alignment.
- `---:` for right alignment.
- `:---:` for centre alignment.

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index="4"}

See [Table basics](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/tables.html) for more.

:::

## Mathematical Expressions

::: {.fragment fragment-index="1"}

**Inline maths:** `$E = mc^2$` renders as $E = mc^2$.

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index="2"}

**Display maths:** Use double dollar signs (on separate lines).

```markdown
$$
E = mc^2
$$
```

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index="4"}

Define custom LaTeX macros in hidden blocks for reuse across your document, see [Markdown Basics - Equations](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/markdown-basics.html#equations)

:::

## Footnotes and References

::: {.fragment fragment-index="1"}

**Standard footnotes:**

```markdown
Here is a footnote reference[^1].

[^1]: Here is the footnote content.
```

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index="2"}

**Inline footnotes:**

```markdown
Here is an inline note^[Much easier to write!].
```

:::

::: {.callout-important .fragment fragment-index="3"}

Footnote identifiers must be unique within the document.

:::

## Figure Basics {.smaller}

::: {.fragment fragment-index="1"}

- Basic

  ```markdown
  ![Elephant](elephant.png)
  ```

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index="2"}

- Size and alignment

  ```markdown
  ![Elephant](elephant.png){width=300}
  ![Elephant](elephant.png){width=80%}
  ![Elephant](elephant.png){width=4in}
  
  ![Elephant](elephant.png){fig-align="left"}
  ```

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index="3"}

- Alternative text and titles

  ```markdown
  ![](elephant.png){fig-alt="A drawing of an elephant."}
  ![Elephant](elephant.png "Title: An elephant"){fig-alt="A drawing of an elephant."}
  ```

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index="4"}

See [Figure basics](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/figures.html) for more.

:::

## Advanced Formatting: Divs and Spans

::: {.fragment fragment-index="1"}

**Divs** for block-level content:

```markdown
::: {#ID .class attribute=value}
This is a "fenced div".
:::
```

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index="2"}

**Spans** for inline formatting:

```markdown
[This is a "span"]{#ID .class attribute=value}
```

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index="3"}

See [Divs and Spans](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/markdown-basics.html#sec-divs-and-spans) for more.

:::

# Quarto Markdown

## Enhanced Markdown Capabilities

Quarto extends standard markdown with powerful features designed specifically for computational documents.

## Shortcodes {.smaller}

### What is a Shortcode?

Shortcodes are special **markdown directives** that **generate various types of content**.

They provide a simple, standardised way to **insert dynamic or complex content** into your Quarto documents without requiring complex markdown syntax or HTML knowledge.

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}

## Shortcodes {.smaller}

:::

### Built-in Shortcodes

::: {#tbl-shortcode tbl-colwidths="[25,75]" style="font-size: 75%;"}

| Shortcode                                                                        | Description                              |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------|
| [version](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/version.html)                        | Print Quarto CLI version.                |
| [var](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/variables.html#var)                      | Print value from `_variables.yml` file.  |
| [meta](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/variables.html#meta)                    | Print value from document metadata.      |
| [env](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/variables.html#env)                      | Print system environment variable.       |
| [pagebreak](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/markdown-basics.html#page-breaks)  | Insert a native page-break.              |
| [kbd](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/markdown-basics.html#keyboard-shortcuts) | Describe keyboard shortcuts.             |
| [video](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/videos.html)                           | Embed a video in a document.             |
| [include](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/includes.html)                       | Include contents of another qmd.         |
| [embed](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/notebook-embed.html)                   | Embed cells from a Jupyter Notebook.     |
| [placeholder](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/placeholder.html)                | Add placeholder images to your document. |
| [lipsum](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/lipsum.html)                          | Add placeholder text to your document.   |
| [contents](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/contents.html)                      | Rearrange content in your document.      |

Shortcodes

:::

## The `include` Shortcode {.smaller}

::: {.fragment fragment-index="1"}

Reuse content across multiple documents effortlessly:

```markdown
{{{< include _content.qmd >}}}
```

:::

::: {layout-ncol="2"}

::: {.fragment fragment-index="2"}

### Key Benefits

- **DRY Principle**: Write once, use everywhere.
- **Consistency**: Shared content stays synchronised.
- **Maintenance**: Update in one place, changes propagate automatically.
- **Modularity**: Break complex documents into manageable pieces.

:::

::: {}

::: {.fragment fragment-index="3"}

### Common Use Cases

- Reusable code.
- Common configuration snippets.

:::

::: {.callout-tip .fragment fragment-index="4"}

Prefix your file or directory with an underscore (`_`) to hide from Quarto's rendering process.

:::

:::

:::

::: {.callout-important .fragment fragment-index="5"}

The `include` shortcode is a plain copy-paste of the file content.
Any YAML header in the included file will replace the current document's YAML header.

:::

## Callout Blocks

::: {.fragment fragment-index="1"}

Five types of callouts for better communication: `note`, `tip`, `warning`, `caution`, `important`.

:::

::: {layout-ncol="2"}

::: {.fragment fragment-index="2"}

```markdown

## Note

Important information for readers.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## Warning

Something to be careful about.
:::
```

## Code Annotations {.smaller}

::: {.fragment fragment-index="1"}

- Source

  ````markdown
  ```r
  library(tidyverse)
  library(palmerpenguins)
  penguins |>                                            # <1>
    mutate(                                              # <2>
      bill_ratio = bill_depth_mm / bill_length_mm,       # <2>
      bill_area  = bill_depth_mm * bill_length_mm        # <2>
    )                                                    # <2>
  ```

  1. Take `penguins`, and then,
  2. add new columns for the bill ratio and bill area.
  ````

:::

::: {layout-ncol="2" layout-valign="center"}

::: {.fragment fragment-index="2"}

- Output

  ```{.r code-line-numbers="1-7|3|4-6"}

      bill_area  = bill_depth_mm * bill_length_mm        # <2>
  ```

## Cross-references: "anything" {.smaller}

::: {.fragment fragment-index="1"}

Define a new custom cross-reference type:

```{.yaml code-line-numbers="1-6|3|4|5"}
crossref:
  custom:
    - kind: float # <1>
      key: txt # <2>
      reference-prefix: Text # <3>
```

1. Cross-referenceable elements with captions are `float`.
2. The identifier prefix used in labels (*e.g.*, `@txt-example`).
3. The text prefix shown in output (*e.g.*, "Text 1").

:::

::: {layout-ncol="2" layout-valign="center"}
::: {.fragment fragment-index="2"}

```markdown
::: {#txt-example}
This is text

This is a caption for the text.
:::

@txt-example is the reference to a text.
```

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index="3"}

::: {#txt-example}
This is text

This is a caption for the text.
:::

@txt-example is the reference to a text.

:::

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index="4"}

See [Custom Float Cross-Reference Types](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/cross-references-custom.html) for more.

:::

## Citations {.smaller}

::: {layout-ncol="2"}

::: {}

::: {.fragment fragment-index="1"}

#### Setup Required

- Bibliography file (`.bib`, `.bibtex`, etc.).
- Optional: CSL file for custom styling.

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index="2"}

#### YAML Configuration

```yaml
bibliography: references.bib
csl: nature.csl  # Optional custom style
```

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index="3"}

#### Bibliography Generation

- Automatic placement at document end.
- Use `## References {#refs}` for custom placement.
- `nocite: "@*"` includes all references.

:::

:::

::: {}

::: {.fragment fragment-index="4"}

#### Citation Syntax

- `[@author2023]` → (Author 2023)
- `[@author2023, p. 15]` → (Author 2023, 15)
- `[@smith2020; @jones2021]` → (Smith 2020; Jones 2021)
- `@author2023 says...` → Author (2023) says...
- `[-@author2023]` → (2023) - suppress author

:::

:::

:::

# YAML Configuration

## Overview {.smaller}

::: {.fragment fragment-index="1"}

The YAML header serves as the configuration hub for your documents, controlling output formats, execution behaviour, and visual presentation.

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index="2"}

**Metadata Inheritance:**

- **Project level**: `_quarto.yml` (*lowest priority*).
- **Directory level**: `_metadata.yml` (*medium priority*).
- **Document level**: YAML header (*highest priority*).

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index="3"}

**Multiple Metadata Files:**

```yaml
metadata-files:
  - _website.yml
  - _common.yml
```

:::

## Document Header

```{.yaml code-line-numbers="|2-4|7-9|10-13|"}
---
title: "My Analysis Report" # <1>
author: "Your Name" # <1>
date: today # <1>
format: 
  html:
    toc: true # <2>
    code-fold: true # <2>
    theme: cosmo # <2>
execute: # <3>
  echo: true # <3>
  warning: false # <3>
  message: false # <3>
---
```

1. Common metadata fields. Option shared by all formats.
2. Option specifically set for HTML output.
3. Global options controlling code execution behaviour.

## Multi-Format Output

Configure multiple output formats simultaneously and share options:

```{.yaml code-line-numbers="|3|10-11|"}
---
title: "Multi-Format Document"
toc: true # <1>
format:
  html:
    theme: flatly
    code-fold: true
    respect-user-color-scheme: true
  pdf:
    documentclass: article  # <2>
    geometry: margin=1in  # <2>
  docx:
    reference-doc: template.docx
---
```

1. Option shared by all formats.
2. Option specifically set for PDF (LaTeX) output.
